name: FAX +49-69/450464
editorial_article:
FAX +49-69/450464, often referred to simply as FAX, was a seminal German independent record label founded in Frankfurt in 1992 by the prolific electronic musician Peter Kuhlmann, known by his alias Pete Namlook. Emerging from the vibrant Frankfurt electronic scene of the early 1990s, the label was established with a philosophy of creative independence and economic efficiency. Kuhlmann, who had worked in banking, applied his analytical mind to the music business, aiming to create a label that bypassed the inefficiencies and exploitative practices he perceived in the industry. The label’s name itself was a functional, idiosyncratic identifier—a fax number that served as the primary contact for fans and collaborators alike.

Musically, FAX was a cornerstone of the ambient, ambient-techno, and space-trance movements. While it began with high-energy trance releases, Namlook’s own evolution shifted the label toward deep, atmospheric ambient music, which he famously distinguished from the "wallpaper" ambient of Brian Eno, viewing his own compositions as emotional journeys. The catalog was characterized by an astonishingly prolific output, with releases often arriving on a near-weekly basis. This volume was supported by Kuhlmann’s rigorous work ethic and his ability to quickly record and finalize projects, often rejecting the "fussy" production habits common among other artists.

Central to the label's cult status was its collaborative spirit. Namlook acted as a pivot point for a wide array of experimental and electronic musicians, including Bill Laswell, Atom TM (Uwe Schmidt), Geir Jennsen (Biosphere), and Richie Hawtin. These collaborations produced hundreds of albums that spanned styles from kosmische to ethno-ambient and dub. The label also gained a reputation for its aesthetic rigor; releases were often color-coded, utilized distinctive inlay art, and were published in strictly limited pressings, making them highly coveted by "ambient completists." Even after Namlook’s passing in 2012, the label remains a monumental reference point for electronic music, serving as a vast archive of 1990s and 2000s experimentalism that rewards deep, persistent archival digging.

citations.title: FAX: Space, Synths and Superhuman Stubbornness | Red Bull Music Academy Daily

editorial_description: Founded by Pete Namlook in Frankfurt in 1992, FAX +49-69/450464 was one of the most prolific and distinctive electronic music labels of the 1990s, renowned for its output of ambient, ambient techno, and experimental electronic music. Its rigid, idiosyncratic business model, highly collectable limited-edition packaging, and Namlook's relentless collaborative spirit defined an entire era of the chillout and space music scene.
